story.title: In Words
story.ofAmount: {who} has {total} {thing} and gives away {taken}/{parts} of them. How many is that?
story.shareLeftover: {cakes} {food} are shared equally between {people} people. How much does each person get?
story.addContext: {who} drinks {left} of a bottle of {drink} and {other} drinks {right} of it. How much is gone?
story.scale: A recipe needs {amount} cups of {thing}. {who} is making {times} times as much. How many cups?
story.compare: {who} fills {big} of a box with {thing} and {other} fills {small} of an identical box. How many times as much does {who} have?
story.multi: {who} has {total} {thing} and gives {taken}/{parts} of them to {other}. Then {who} finds {extra} more. How many now?
story.missAmount: Cut the whole amount into the groups the bottom number asks for, then take that many groups.
story.missShare: The one left over does not stay left over. It gets cut up and shared as well.
story.missAdd: Both pieces have to be the same size before they can be counted together.
story.missScale: The whole ones and the fraction both get multiplied. Neither one stays behind.
story.missCompare: How many times as much is a division. Taking one away from the other answers a different question.
story.missMulti: There are two steps here. Work out the first one, then do the second to that answer.
story.rightAmount: Cut the {whole} into {parts} equal groups and take {shaded} of them — that is {expected}.
story.rightShare: Everybody gets a whole one first, and what is left is cut between them — {expected} each.
story.rightAdd: Cut both into the same-sized pieces and count them together: {expected} of the bottle.
story.rightScale: Multiply the whole cups and the part cups, then gather the parts into whole ones — {expected}.
story.rightCompare: Ask how many of the smaller fill the larger, and the answer is {expected} times as much.
story.rightMulti: Give some away first, then add what turned up afterwards — {expected} at the end.
story.hintAmount1: The bottom number says how many equal groups the whole amount makes.
story.hintAmount2: Cut the bar into that many, and work out how many are in one group.
story.hintAmount3: Then take as many groups as the top number asks for.
story.hintShare1: Give everybody a whole one first, and see what is left over.
story.hintShare2: The leftover does not stay left over — it gets cut up and shared too.
story.hintShare3: So each person gets some whole ones and a fraction of one more.
story.hintAdd1: Two amounts of the same bottle, so they can be added — once they match.
story.hintAdd2: Cut both into the same-sized pieces first.
story.hintAdd3: Then count the pieces that are gone.
story.hintScale1: Both bits of the amount get multiplied: the whole cups and the part cups.
story.hintScale2: Do the whole cups first, then the parts.
story.hintScale3: If the parts make more than a whole cup, that cup joins the others.
story.hintCompare1: This asks how many times as much, which is a dividing question.
story.hintCompare2: Ask how many of the smaller amount fit inside the bigger one.
story.hintCompare3: Taking one away from the other answers a different question — how much more.
story.hintMulti1: There are two things happening here, one after the other.
story.hintMulti2: Work out the fraction step first and write down what is left.
story.hintMulti3: Then do the second step to that answer, not to the number you started with.
story.cutToMatch: cut the bar to match the story, then answer
story.emptyBar: an empty bar to model the story on
story.methodShare1: Give everybody a whole one first.
story.methodShare2: Then cut what is left between them — the leftover does not stay left over.
story.methodCompare1: How many times as much is a dividing question.
story.methodCompare2: How much more is a taking-away question. Read which one is being asked.

route.title: Which Way?
route.matchLabel: Just count them — the pieces already match
route.smallLabel: Find the smallest size they both fit
route.simpLabel: Cut them down before doing anything
route.benchLabel: Judge it against a half first
route.matchWhy: Both are {words} already, so nothing needs cutting up.
route.oneWhy: {small} goes into {big} exactly, so only the {words} need cutting up.
route.multWhy: {a} and {b} share no factor, so {product} is the size to use.
route.smallWhy: They share a factor of {shared}, so the pieces can be smaller than {product}.
route.simpWhy: {messy} is {simple} in simpler terms, which makes everything after it easier.
route.benchWhy: {near} is about a half, so you know roughly what the answer should be before you start.
route.prompt: {a} + {b}. Which way would you do it?
route.hint1: Look at the two bottom numbers before you look at anything else.
route.hint2: Are they the same? Does one go into the other? Do they share a factor?
route.hint3: More than one way can be right here. Pick one that suits these particular numbers.
route.missWrong: That one does not suit these particular numbers. Look at the two bottom numbers again.
route.missDefault: That route suits these two numbers.
route.moreThanOne: more than one of these can be right
route.print: {a} + {b}. Which way would you do this one, and why?
route.method1: Look at the two bottom numbers first.
route.method2: The same? Nothing to cut. One goes into the other? Cut only one of them.
route.method3: Sharing a factor? The pieces can be smaller than multiplying the bottoms would give.
